rows.text: Gaddock Teeg turns off the top half of every noncreature card in the format: no wrath, no Cyclonic Rift, no Torment of Hailfire, no big X draw spell, no Approach of the Second Sun. The deck is built so that constraint is entirely one-sided — every removal effect here is either stapled to a creature or costs three or less, so you keep answering things while the table cannot.

rows.name: Gaddock Teeg
rows.text: two mana. No noncreature spell with mana value four or more can be cast by anyone, and no noncreature spell with {X} in its cost at all. He is a 2/2, so protect him; he is also the single most warping card the deck has.
Note what he does NOT stop: creature spells of any size, and permanents already on the battlefield. That is why the deck's own threats are all creatures.

rows.name: Conqueror's Flail
rows.text: opponents cannot cast spells during your turn at all while it is attached. Teeg stops the expensive answers; the Flail stops the cheap ones.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: the same lockout on a body.

rows.name: Dosan the Falling Leaf
rows.text: players can cast spells only during their own turns. With Teeg out, an opponent's window to answer anything shrinks to their own main phase, at three mana or less.

rows.name: City of Solitude
rows.text: the enchantment version, harder to remove.

guide.title: Removal that survives your own lock

rows.text: Every one of these is a creature or costs three or less, which is the whole design constraint.

rows.name: Aura Shards
rows.text: the engine. Every creature you play destroys an artifact or enchantment, and Teeg means they cannot wrath your creatures away to stop it.

rows.name: Acidic Slime
rows.text: an artifact, enchantment OR land, on a deathtouch blocker.

rows.name: Bane of Progress
rows.text: destroys EVERY artifact and enchantment on the board and grows for each. Your own board is creatures, so it is close to one-sided.

rows.name: Knight of Autumn
rows.text: removal, life, or a 4/3 — pick what the board needs.

rows.name: Duplicant
rows.text: exiles a creature permanently and becomes it.

rows.name: Meteor Golem
rows.text: destroys any nonland permanent. Seven mana, but it is a creature, so Teeg lets you cast it.

rows.name: Path to Exile
rows.text: one mana, exile.

rows.name: Get Lost
rows.text: two mana for a creature, enchantment or planeswalker.

rows.name: Generous Gift
rows.text: three mana for literally any permanent.

rows.name: Beast Within
rows.text: the instant-speed version.

rows.name: Krosan Grip
rows.text: split second, so it beats the response.

rows.name: Nature's Claim
rows.text: one mana for any artifact or enchantment.

rows.name: Aura of Silence
rows.text: taxes their artifacts and enchantments, then eats one.

rows.name: Archon of Emeria
rows.text: one spell per turn each, and their nonbasics enter tapped.

rows.name: Drannith Magistrate
rows.text: no casting from graveyards, exile or the command zone.

rows.name: Linvala, Keeper of Silence
rows.text: their creature abilities stop working.

rows.name: Collector Ouphe
rows.text: their artifact abilities stop working.

rows.name: Kataki, War's Wage
rows.text: every artifact costs its controller {1} a turn to keep. Against an artifact deck it is a slow Armageddon.

rows.name: Containment Priest
rows.text: anything entering without being cast is exiled — reanimation, blink and cheat-into-play all stop.

rows.name: Grafdigger's Cage
rows.text: nothing comes back from graveyards or libraries.

rows.name: Aven Mindcensor
rows.text: flash him onto a fetchland or tutor.

rows.name: Archivist of Oghma
rows.text: a card and a life every time anyone searches.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell each turn.

rows.name: Ghostly Prison
rows.text: they pay per attacker, which matters because Teeg is a 2/2 and the deck is slow to block.

rows.name: Beast Whisperer
rows.text: a card for every creature spell, which is most of the deck.

rows.name: Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines
rows.text: your enter triggers happen twice and theirs do not happen at all. It doubles Aura Shards, Acidic Slime, Bane of Progress, Knight of Autumn and Craterhoof simultaneously.

rows.name: Archivist of Oghma
rows.text: cards off their tutors.

rows.name: Birds of Paradise
rows.text: turn-one fixing.

rows.name: Avacyn's Pilgrim
rows.text: the white half.

rows.name: Llanowar Elves
rows.text: the green half.

rows.name: Elvish Mystic
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: Bloom Tender
rows.text: two colours off one tap.

rows.name: Delighted Halfling
rows.text: uncounterable mana for legendary spells, which covers Teeg himself.

rows.name: Nature's Lore
rows.text: an untapped dual with a basic type.

rows.name: Cultivate
rows.text: a land down and a land in hand.
This is the question a Teeg deck has to answer, and the answer is that everything lethal here is a creature.

rows.name: Craterhoof Behemoth
rows.text: the standard ending on a board of hatebears.

rows.name: End-Raze Forerunners
rows.text: the second copy, with vigilance and haste for the whole team.

rows.name: Avenger of Zendikar
rows.text: a Plant for every land you control, then counters on all of them per landfall.

rows.name: Adeline, Resplendent Cathar
rows.text: a body per opponent on every attack, and her power counts the whole board.

rows.name: Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
rows.text: +2/+2 to yours and -2/-2 to theirs, which is a one-sided wrath that keeps attacking afterwards.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a mana dork and Teeg. Turn-one acceleration into a turn-two Teeg is the strongest start in the deck, and every turn he is out is a turn the table cannot cast its best cards.
Protect him over developing. Teeg is a 2/2 that every opponent wants dead, and the lock is worth far more than one extra hatebear on the battlefield.

rows.name: Aura Shards
rows.text: prioritise it. Teeg already stops them casting the wrath that would clear your creatures, so Aura Shards becomes a removal spell on every single creature you play for the rest of the game.
Remember Teeg binds you too. There are no X spells and no expensive noncreature cards in the deck on purpose — if you ever want one, it has to be a creature.
